title: Box-WAM: Box Trajectories as Compact State Representations for World Action Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.17526v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: World action models (WAMs) are a category of policy models that ex- plicitly predict both actions and future world states. They have been shown to outperform action-only models across various robotic manipulation tasks. How- ever, representing the future with full-frame video prediction can be computation- ally expensive during both training and inference. This raises a central question: what compact state representation preserves the planning and supervision bene- fits of future prediction? In this paper, we propose BoxWAM, which replaces dense future frames with oriented bounding box trajectories of task-relevant ob- jects. By explicitly imagining object-centric future motion, our method provides a lightweight prediction target that captures the key physical changes induced by robot actions. translated_title: Box-WAM：以边界框轨迹作为世界动作模型的紧凑状态表示
translated_abstract: 世界动作模型（WAMs）是一类显式预测动作和未来世界状态的策略模型。已有研究表明，在多种机器人操作任务中，它们的表现优于仅预测动作的模型。然而，使用全帧视频预测来表示未来状态，在训练和推理阶段都可能带来高昂的计算成本。这就引出了一个核心问题：什么样的紧凑状态表示既能保留未来预测在规划与监督方面的优势？在本文中，我们提出了BoxWAM，它用任务相关物体的带方向边界框轨迹取代密集的未来视频帧。通过显式地想象以物体为中心的未来运动，我们的方法提供了一个轻量级的预测目标，能够捕捉机器人动作所引发的关键物理变化。我们证明，边界框轨迹预测在大幅降低计算成本的同时提升了动作预测性能，这表明……
tldr: BoxWAM用任务相关物体的带方向边界框轨迹替代密集的未来视频帧作为世界动作模型的紧凑状态表示，在大幅降低计算成本的同时提升了机器人动作预测性能。
en_tdlr: BoxWAM replaces dense future video frames with oriented bounding box trajectories of task-relevant objects as compact state representations for world action models, substantially reducing computational cost while improving action prediction performance.
